items.readable_text:
Content:
The five congruence criteria for triangles are often needed when proving geometric results. Therefore, it's essential to identify which congruence criterion is being applied in a particular situation.

Content:
Let's start by briefly reviewing the five criteria that we have learned.

Content:
- The Side-Side-Side (SSS) criterion: Two triangles are congruent if and only if three sides of one triangle are congruent to three sides of the other triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3c0b217a542d0c7c43d0a670edb35b5f]

Content:
- The Side-Angle-Side (SAS) criterion: Two triangles are congruent if and only if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are congruent to two sides and the included angle of the other triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fa75509038c66b2fe8ab6fb94c03a993]

Content:
- The Angle-Side-Angle (ASA) criterion: Two triangles are congruent if and only if two angles and the included side of one triangle are congruent to two angles and the included side of the other triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fb402a31aeabf543777a72bb52fe01d6]

Content:
- The Angle-Angle-Side (AAS) criterion: Two triangles are congruent if and only if two angles and the non-included side of one triangle are congruent to two angles and the non-included side of the other triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/55cd87ef4ed66db5b50f4710842f3226]

Content:
- The Hypotenuse-Leg (HL) criterion: Two right triangles are congruent if and only if they have congruent hypotenuses and a pair of congruent legs.

[IMG: /graphics/b21864ec072a8bcf9efc842f4ccf3e38]

Content:
Let's now get some practice at correctly identifying these criteria.

items.title: Identifying Congruent Triangles

sections.normalized_html: By which congruence criterion does it follow that [MATH: \triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF?]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/cc0870c486985a310c6c2a68996b4424]

By which congruence criterion does it follow that [MATH: \triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we recall the ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) congruence criterion:

Two triangles are congruent if and only if two angles and the included side of one triangle are congruent to two angles and the included side of the other triangle.

Now, we have [MATH: \underbrace{\angle A \cong \angle D}_{\textrm{Angle}}, \qquad \underbrace{\overline{AB}\cong \overline{DE}}_{\textrm{(included) Side}}, \qquad \underbrace{\angle B \cong \angle E}_{\textrm{Angle}}.]

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle ABC] and [MATH: \triangle DEF] are congruent by ASA.
sections.readable_text:

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle ABC] and [MATH: \triangle DEF] are congruent by ASA.

sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we recall the HL (Hypotenuse-Leg) congruence criterion:

Two right triangles are congruent if and only if they have congruent hypotenuses and a pair of congruent legs.

Notice that the triangles have a common side, [MATH: \overline{AB}.] To determine which criterion applies, it's helpful to think of this as two separate triangles, as shown below.

Next, we have [MATH: \underbrace{m\angle{C} = m\angle{D} = 90^\circ}_{\textrm{Right angle}}\,, \qquad \underbrace{\overline{AB} \cong \overline{AB}}_{\textrm{Hypotenuse}}\,, \qquad \underbrace{\overline{BC}\cong \overline{BD}}_{\textrm{Leg}}\,.]

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle ABC] and [MATH: \triangle ABD] are congruent by HL.

Content:
The SAS congruence criterion states that if two triangles have two pairs of congruent sides and the included angles are also congruent, the triangles are congruent.

Content:
Why, then, is there no SSA congruence criterion? In other words, if two triangles have two pairs of congruent sides and a pair of congruent non-included angles, why is this not enough to conclude that they're congruent?

To understand why there is no SSA criterion, we'll construct two triangles that are not congruent yet have two pairs of congruent sides and a pair of congruent, non-included angles.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The five congruence criteria for triangles are often needed when proving geometric results. Therefore, it's essential to identify which congruence criterion is being applied in a particular situation.

Content:
Let's start by briefly reviewing the five criteria that we have learned.

Content:
- The Side-Side-Side (SSS) criterion: Two triangles are congruent if and only if three sides of one triangle are congruent to three sides of the other triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3c0b217a542d0c7c43d0a670edb35b5f]

Content:
- The Side-Angle-Side (SAS) criterion: Two triangles are congruent if and only if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are congruent to two sides and the included angle of the other triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fa75509038c66b2fe8ab6fb94c03a993]

Content:
- The Angle-Side-Angle (ASA) criterion: Two triangles are congruent if and only if two angles and the included side of one triangle are congruent to two angles and the included side of the other triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fb402a31aeabf543777a72bb52fe01d6]

Content:
- The Angle-Angle-Side (AAS) criterion: Two triangles are congruent if and only if two angles and the non-included side of one triangle are congruent to two angles and the non-included side of the other triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/55cd87ef4ed66db5b50f4710842f3226]

Content:
- The Hypotenuse-Leg (HL) criterion: Two right triangles are congruent if and only if they have congruent hypotenuses and a pair of congruent legs.

[IMG: /graphics/b21864ec072a8bcf9efc842f4ccf3e38]

Content:
Let's now get some practice at correctly identifying these criteria.

---

\qquad

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle ABC] and [MATH: \triangle DEF] are congruent by ASA.

[MATH: \underbrace{m\angle{C} = m\angle{D} = 90^\circ}_{\textrm{Right angle}}\,, \qquad
\underbrace{\overline{AB} \cong \overline{AB}}_{\textrm{Hypotenuse}}\,, \qquad \underbrace{\overline{BC}\cong \overline{BD}}_{\textrm{Leg}}\,.]

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle ABC] and [MATH: \triangle ABD] are congruent by HL.

Item 12 — Tutorial: Why Is There No SSA Criterion?

The SAS congruence criterion states that if two triangles have two pairs of congruent sides and the included angles are also congruent, the triangles are congruent.
